audit.whatIsWrong: The whole entry is built on waiting for Permafrost to be on cooldown. tldr, winCon, focus, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], wants.you[1], whys[3], early and mid all say some version of "trade when her E is down" or "all-in when either is down".
audit.why: Permafrost's cooldown is 1.5 seconds. It is never down. Riot's text is "Sejuani freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks" — the ability is gated by the Frost gauge on YOU, not by a cooldown, which is why she can hold it indefinitely and fire it the instant the fourth stack lands. An entry that tells the reader to wait for a 1.5s cooldown is telling them to wait for nothing, and it hides the thing they can actually control: how many stacks they are carrying when they step up. The cooldowns that do matter are Winter's Wrath at 9s down to 5s, because that is what stacks them, and Arctic Assault at 18s at rank 1, because that is her only engage.
audit.corrected: Repointed from the ability to the Frost gauge across tldr, winCon, focus.text, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], spikes[0] and early; Arctic Assault's 18s named as the real punish window in wants.you[1], whys[3] and mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (E cd 1.5; W cd 9/8/7/6/5; Q cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive passive interactions are absent. Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, and Fury of the North lets Sejuani shatter a stunned enemy for massive magic damage. Neither is stated as an interaction anywhere; whys[0] and early mention Frost Armor's "slow-immunity" in passing but never connect it to Lacerate, and the shatter is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: "After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows... Sejuani can damage a stunned enemy to shatter it, dealing massive magic damage." Ambessa's only sticking tool is Lacerate's slow, and Frost Armor turns it off outright — so the dash is her disengage here, not the slow. And the shatter means every stun in the matchup, Permafrost or Glacial Prison, is not just lost time but the largest damage instance in Sejuani's kit. The entry instead attributes her damage to "her W is physical % max HP damage and her passive adds 10% max HP magic on a stunned target", numbers that appear nowhere in Riot's text.
audit.corrected: Slow immunity tied to Lacerate in spikes[2], early, wants.foe[1], whys[0] and dosFull[1]; the shatter written into mid, late, dontsFull[0] and report[5]; the unsupported percentage figures removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Arctic Assault is called "her Q dash" and treated as a mobility tool. It is a knockup, and the entry never says so.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sejuani charges forward, knocking enemies into the air. The charge stops after hitting an enemy champion." Two consequences the entry misses — it is hard CC on arrival, which then arms the passive shatter, and it stops dead on the first champion it touches, so it cannot be used to run past you. At 18s at rank 1 it is by far the longest non-ultimate cooldown in her kit and the correct thing to bait.
audit.corrected: Named as a knockup with its 18s cooldown and its stop-on-first-champion behaviour in mid, whys[3], wants.you[1] and dontsFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Seven strings credit Public Execution with "the R passive's flat armor pen" or "its armor-pen passive" — spikes[1], spikes[2], mid, late, whys[4], whys[5] and wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Public Execution blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. It has no armour penetration, and Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund rather than penetration. Against a champion who builds Frozen Heart and Sunfire this is the worst possible place to invent penetration, because it tells the reader their burst still works after she itemises when the entry's own late paragraph says it does not.
audit.corrected: Removed from every string I touched and replaced with the crash stun and Glacial Prison's 120s cooldown as the real reasons the level-6 all-in converts.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and the spike list carries no cooldown numbers despite the lane being decided by two of them.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield; Repudiation is Ambessa's only shield. The real spike shape here is Arctic Assault at 18s and Glacial Prison at 120s against Ambessa's level-6 Public Execution — two long enemy cooldowns and one long friendly one, which is why this is a 55.19% lane that still has to be closed before Sejuani finishes tank items.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected; real numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns, whys[3], whys[4] and the do/don't descriptions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Ambessa level 1 while whys[0] opens "Even at 1", gives Skill at level 6 while whys[4] calls it a guaranteed all-in, and gives Ambessa the two-item stage while whys[6] says the threat moves off the lane and to close before then.
audit.why: 55.19% over 212 games is a genuinely favourable lane, and the packet levelChart (Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill) matches the prose: even at 1 because Frost Armor is up and Ambessa has one ability, Ambessa's from 2 through first item, and back to even once Sejuani is a tank with a teamfight ultimate.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Ambessa" is 7 characters and "Skill" is 5, so all three flips cross the length band. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate that does not match their titles, and the same three don't-strings are concatenated into report[11] as Common Mistakes.
audit.why: Each has a real answer here: Frost Armor's slow immunity is why weaving out beats slowing, Drakehound's Step needs a cast to fire, Arctic Assault knocks up into the passive shatter, and Glacial Prison reaches 1300 units.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten against the kit.

edits.before: Q-cone into Sundering Slam plus a Drakehound's Step dash gives you a real short-trade combo. Sejuani's only point of CC, the Permafrost E, needs four Frost stacks on you first, so trade before she has stacked you and step out with your dash.
edits.after: Q-cone into Sundering Slam plus a Drakehound's Step dash gives you a real short-trade combo. Permafrost is on a 1.5s cooldown, so it is never down — the only thing gating her stun is the Frost gauge. Trade before it fills, then dash out.

edits.before: Public Execution blinks you behind her and suppresses + stuns through her resists, and the R passive's flat armor pen makes the slam hurt. It is your first guaranteed kill window the moment her Glacial Prison is on cooldown.
edits.after: Public Execution blinks to her and suppresses, and the crash stun finishes it. Glacial Prison is 120s at rank 1 — the moment it is spent she has one 18s knockup left and no real way to answer your all-in.

edits.before: Eclipse plus the level-9 Q max: Q1-auto-Q2 chunks her, and your R's flat armor pen cuts straight through the early armor she stacks before she has a full tank build online.
edits.after: Eclipse plus the level-9 Q max: Q1-auto-Q2 chunks her before Frozen Heart and Sunfire land, and Frost Armor's slow immunity is the only thing blanking your Lacerate.

edits.before: Sejuani's only hard lockdown is the Permafrost E, and it does not fire until she has stacked four Frost on you with autos and Winter's Wrath — so watch that gauge and trade before it fills. Level 1 is even: her Frost Armor gives her bonus resists and slow-immunity once she takes damage, and you only have one ability online. From level 2-3 your Q cone into Sundering Slam plus a Drakehound's Step dash lets you weave an empowered auto and pull back before she can stack you up. Trade when her Frost stacks on you are low and her E is down — if you are sitting on four stacks with her E up, respect the stun and back off.
edits.after: Sejuani's only hard lockdown is Permafrost, and it does not fire until she has stacked four Frost on you with autos and Winter's Wrath — so watch that gauge, because its cooldown is 1.5s and will never save you. Level 1 is even: Frost Armor comes from being out of combat and grants armour, magic resist and slow immunity, so your Lacerate slow does nothing until it breaks. From level 2-3 your Q cone into Sundering Slam plus a Drakehound's Step dash lets you weave an empowered auto and pull back before she can stack you. Never sit on four stacks in her range.

edits.before: This is your lane. Sejuani's engage is her Q dash (Arctic Assault) and her lockdown is the Permafrost E — punish the windows when either is on cooldown. Dash-weave Q1-auto-Q2 and crash empowered hits while she cannot stun you. At 6 your R is the difference-maker: Public Execution blinks behind her, suppresses and stuns through her resists, and its passive armor-pen makes the slam land hard, so the moment her Glacial Prison is down you have a guaranteed all-in. Don't let her build four Frost stacks on you for free — her W is physical % max HP damage and her passive adds 10% max HP magic on a stunned target, so a full Permafrost chain hurts even on a tank.
edits.after: This is your lane. Her engage is Arctic Assault, an 18s knockup at rank 1 that stops on the first champion it hits, and once it is spent she cannot start anything for the better part of twenty seconds — that is the window. Dash-weave Q1-auto-Q2 and crash empowered hits while your Frost gauge is low. At 6 your R is the difference-maker: Public Execution blinks to her, suppresses and stuns, so the moment Glacial Prison is down you have a guaranteed all-in. And never eat the stun: Fury of the North lets her shatter a stunned target for massive magic damage, which is where the real burst in her kit lives.

edits.before: You out-1v1 her all game, but she is a tank with a teamfight ult, so the threat moves off the lane. She'll stack Frozen Heart and Sunfire, and your damage is entirely physical — even with your R's flat armor-pen, a fully-itemized Sejuani is a wall. Snowball your lead into objectives and her tower early; don't expect to delete her once she's tanked up. In fights, dodge her Glacial Prison and the empowered-R slow zone, and don't waste your R blinking onto her when a squishy is the real target.
edits.after: You out-1v1 her all game, but she is a tank with a teamfight ult, so the threat moves off the lane. She'll stack Frozen Heart and Sunfire and your damage is entirely physical, so a fully-itemized Sejuani is a wall. Snowball your lead into objectives and her tower early; don't expect to delete her once she's tanked up. In fights, dodge Glacial Prison — one stun and Fury of the North shatters you — and don't waste your R blinking onto her when a squishy is the real target.

notes:
The packet reports zero defects and six sequencing cues for this matchup, which made it look clean. It was not: every one of those cues pointed at Permafrost's cooldown, and Permafrost's cooldown is 1.5 seconds. A cue-counting check cannot tell "wait for her E" from "wait for her E, which is always up" — worth knowing if the sequencing-cue metric is being used to prioritise work elsewhere.

Two unsupported numbers removed from mid: "her W is physical % max HP damage" and "her passive adds 10% max HP magic on a stunned target". Riot's text for Winter's Wrath says only damage, slow and Frost stacks, and for Fury of the North says "massive magic damage" with no figure. I replaced them with the mechanic rather than inventing a corrected number.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: content win[0], win[4], win[6] and full phases[0].side, phases[4].side, phases[6].side should read Skill, Ambessa, Skill respectively — matching the packet levelChart and this entry's own whys[0], whys[4] and whys[6]. CHAMPION-LEVEL FABRICATION, appears seven more times here: "R passive armor-pen". Public Execution has no penetration. Also still outstanding across the champion: "Medarda Maxim", a non-existent Ambessa passive, 6 occurrences in champ-data/content/ambessa.js.
